# Combine XYZ

Builds a position or direction from separate X, Y and Z values.

`lfs.combine_xyz` · Utilities

## How to use

Use to change one coordinate while keeping the other two.\
Connect the result to a Vector input.

## Inputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| X | `X` | lfs.float | 0 | step 0.01; accepts per-element values | X coordinate in the units you need. 0, the default, gives no contribution along this axis. |
| Y | `Y` | lfs.float | 0 | step 0.01; accepts per-element values | Y coordinate in the units you need. 0, the default, gives no contribution along this axis. |
| Z | `Z` | lfs.float | 0 | step 0.01; accepts per-element values | Z coordinate in the units you need. 0, the default, gives no contribution along this axis. |

## Outputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vector | `Vector` | lfs.vector | — | — | Resulting X, Y and Z values, in the units of your calculation. |
